title.value: Collective Decision Making by Embodied Neural Agents
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated at the beginning of the paper and captures the essence of the research, which involves neural agents making collective decisions through embodied interactions.
title.quote: Collective decision making by embodied neural agents

analysis.description: This paper investigates the neural dynamics involved in collective decision making among embodied agents. By utilizing simple neural models and embedding agents in a stimulus environment, the study explores how sensorimotor coordination within agents and social interaction between them can lead to collective decisions. The research ties these dynamics to environmental and agent-based factors, contributing insights relevant to neuro-AI and self-organized multi-agent systems.

type.justification: The paper involves simulations and experiments with agents in a controlled environment, measuring performance and dynamics, which is characteristic of empirical research.
type.quote: we performed both single-agent simulations and multi-agent simulations. For the single-agent simulations, we quantified neural coordination dynamics in terms of integration and metastability.

name.justification: The research focuses on collective behaviors and decision-making processes amongst multiple agents, fitting the multi-agent systems domain.
name.quote: Collective decision making using simple social interactions has been studied in many types of multi-agent systems, including robot swarms and human social networks.

name.justification: The research incorporates neural dynamics as part of decision making and coordination among agents, indicating a focus on neurodynamics.
name.quote: The neural mechanisms that enable such coordination among embodied biological agents are currently not well understood.

name.justification: The study emphasizes the role of embodiment in decision-making and neural interaction, aligning with the principles of embodied cognition.
name.quote: Largely inspired by the enactive approach to embodied cognition, we constructed minimalist agents that simulate important attributes of biological agents.

name.justification: The research falls into swarm intelligence due to its exploration of collective decision making and interaction within groups.
name.quote: Our findings make the case for the inclusion of intrinsic neural dynamics in the development of artificial intelligence and multi-agent systems, as a means to expand their ability for social interactions and collective tasks.

name.justification: The study specifically uses the HKB equations to model agent dynamics, as highlighted in the text discussing the agent design and modeling approach.
name.quote: The Haken-Kelso-Bunz (HKB) equations provide a straightforward way to model metastable dynamics among interacting components.

is_contributed.justification: The HKB model is used as a foundation for the study rather than being developed or modified significantly within the scope of this paper.
is_contributed.quote: The Haken-Kelso-Bunz (HKB) equations provide a straightforward way to model metastable dynamics among interacting components.

is_executed.justification: The model was executed as part of the simulation experiments to study agent behavior and neural dynamics.
is_executed.quote: The Haken-Kelso-Bunz (HKB) equations were first implemented as a neural controller of an embodied agent by Aguilera et al. [2013].

is_compared.justification: There is no indication that the HKB equations were compared with other models within the scope of this research. The focus was on examining their application.
is_compared.quote: We adopted the HKB agent of Aguilera et al. [2013] and modified it so that it could support embodied collective decision making.

referenced_paper_title.value: A theoretical model of phase transitions in human hand movements
referenced_paper_title.justification: The HKB model is referenced in the study as originally developed by Haken, Kelso, and Bunz.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Haken, J. A. Scott Kelso, and H. Bunz. A theoretical model of phase transitions in human hand movements. Biological Cybernetics, 51(5):347–356, feb 1985.

name.justification: PyTorch was explicitly mentioned as the library used for implementing the agents in the simulation.
name.quote: Simulations were performed in Python version 3.9.2 [Van Rossum and Drake, 2009] and the agents were implemented in Pytorch version 1.12.0.
